A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multiscale CNN training work despite substantial revisions and a changed title. Their complete texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained algorithms and results can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original blur-estimation experiments, image-reconstruction benchmarks, runtime measurements, and supplementary analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original image-reconstruction results, loss-evaluation timings, subsampling comparisons, and computational-budget and resolution-level experiments in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: v3 removes the learnable PDE-based Mesh-Free Convolutions (MFCs) proposed in v2 Section 3, eliminating an entire model component. The multilevel gradient estimator and coarse-to-fine training procedure remain under the names MGE and Full-Multiscale; their renaming does not itself change the method.

E1.justification: The four image-recovery tasks on STL10, CelebA, and Urban100 remain, including the matched deeper-network denoising experiment. v2's separately documented synthetic blur-kernel estimation task using random Markov fields disappears. v3's fixed-budget table does not identify an additional dataset or task.

E2.justification: The MFC architecture comparisons and the FNO-ESPCN comparator in v2 Table 7 are removed. v3 Table 2 introduces cropping-only and combined cropping/coarsening Full-Multiscale alternatives across all four recovery tasks, substantially changing the comparison methods. Single-scale training remains the principal baseline.

E3.justification: v3 introduces cropping controls, fixed-WU budgets, two- and three-level configurations, and CPU loss timing over 512 STL10 images. The gradient diagnostic replaces the smooth/unit-Gaussian example with a noise-scale sweep from 0 to 0.5. v3 Table 7 also reports cosine annealing instead of v2 Table 10's constant learning rate for denoising, deblurring, and inpainting; this reporting change does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds coarsening-versus-cropping comparisons, matched-compute performance analysis, and resolution-level sensitivity tests (Tables 2, 5, and 6), and revises the noise-gradient analysis. v2's blur-estimation convergence case and CNN/MFC feature-map study are removed. The standard deeper-network analysis is retained.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix D.5 explicitly averages convolution runtimes over 500 operations; that study and its repetition information disappear. v3 Figure 2 introduces shaded bands without defining their statistical meaning or reporting a repetition count. Neither version specifies repeated-training uncertainty or seed variation.

E6.justification: New subsampling, timing, fixed-budget, noise, and resolution-level results replace substantial MFC, FNO, and blur-estimation results. Main denoising, deblurring, and inpainting scores are retained. Under the unchanged documented super-resolution setup, reported ESPCN SSIM changes from 0.8491 to 0.8629 for single-scale training and from 0.8042 to 0.8274 for Full-Multiscale (v2 Table 4; v3 Table 2); these are updated results, not an established method improvement.

T1.justification: v3 removes the MFC convergence and expressivity lemmas and associated PDE derivations. It replaces the one-dimensional Taylor argument with a bounded, Lipschitz pixel-gradient proof, adds coarsening-versus-cropping error bounds (Appendix B), and develops a two-level equal-accuracy computational-cost derivation. The retained hot-start convergence argument gains explicit smoothness and convexity assumptions.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from multiscale training plus a new mesh-independent convolution family to gradient estimation and coarse-to-fine initialization for existing CNNs. v3 drops the MFC novelty and convergence contributions and adds theoretically justified coarsening over cropping to its concluding claims.

C2.justification: v2 uses noisy-gradient behavior to motivate MFCs and presents a standard-convolution failure case. Based on a revised noise experiment, v3 instead argues that cross-resolution gradients remain sufficiently close for practical standard-CNN training. It adds interpretations favoring coarsening over cropping and explicitly excludes attention from its theoretical guarantees, while removing the feature-map smoothing explanation.

D1.justification: v3 deletes the MFC FFT implementation, periodic-boundary specifications, and MFC architecture and parameter-count details from v2 Section 3 and Appendix E. It specifies batch allocations for the new timing experiment and revises learning-rate documentation. Most standard-CNN specifications and the promise to release code upon acceptance remain.

R1.justification: v3 abandons the differential-operator positioning of MFCs and their claimed expressivity advantage relative to FNO, centering the contribution on MLMC-inspired training of existing CNNs. Associated MFC literature is removed, while dataset references for STL10, CelebA, and Urban100 are added. Much of the multigrid and multiscale-training background remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, conclusion, and substantial explanatory passages are rewritten, and Multiscale-SGD is renamed MGE. The MFC section disappears, the Full-Multiscale discussion is expanded and repositioned, and the appendices are reorganized around revised proofs and analyses. This is extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Tables are redesigned with subsampling columns and color highlighting; MFC-related illustrations are removed, and noise and coarsening figures are added. v3 Figure 3 combines four existing image cases from v2 Appendix F, while other cases remain in the appendix with MFC columns removed.

improvement.justification: v3 improves focus, makes convergence assumptions explicit, and adds useful subsampling and resolution-level controls. However, it removes v2's blur-estimation failure analysis while adopting a more favorable interpretation of noisy standard CNNs. The revised noise plot uses a squared-norm axis despite an unsquared definition, and the fixed-budget study omits its task and backbone. These evidential gains and reporting weaknesses prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
